# V1 getting started

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-v1-guides.ts from executed canonical source. Do not edit this output by hand. -->

Fadeno V1 is a working private framework, not yet a registry release. This
guide uses the [canonical packed application](../../examples/v1-app/README.md),
whose check, build, development, production start, routes, failures, and
recovery are executed by the local merge gate.

## Requirements and current boundary

Use Node.js 22.17 or newer and the repository's locked package manager. From a
clean checkout, install with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. There is no public
package name, scaffold command, deployment command, or compatibility promise
yet; A0 owns those release decisions.

The example package is the executable command contract. `pnpm build` runs the
transactional production build, `pnpm dev` starts the retained loopback
development server on its explicit port, and `pnpm start` starts an accepted
production build.

```json
{
  "name": "fadeno-v1-app-example",
  "version": "0.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "fadeno build --project-root .",
    "dev": "fadeno dev --project-root . --port 4173",
    "start": "node --import ./dist/.fadeno/routes/loader.js ./dist/server/bootstrap.js"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "fadeno-framework-internal": "workspace:*"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/node": "22.20.1",
    "typescript": "7.0.2"
  }
}
```

## Configure routes

The configuration uses the public package entrypoint and chooses the directory
that owns route files.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "fadeno-framework-internal";

export default defineConfig({ routes: { root: "src/routes" } });
```

## Add a layout and page

Route files are ordinary TypeScript/TSX. The root layout owns the document
shell, while the root page reads request-owned resources and returns HTML-shaped
JSX. The generated route module and stock TypeScript own route typing.

```tsx
import type { Layout } from "fadeno-framework-internal";

const layout: Layout = ({ children }) => (
  <html lang="en">
    <head>
      <title>Fadeno V1 application</title>
    </head>
    <body>
      <header>
        <nav aria-label="Primary">
          <a href="/">Home</a>
          <a href="/hello/Fadeno">Greeting</a>
        </nav>
      </header>
      <main>{children}</main>
      <footer>Rendered by the V1 framework</footer>
    </body>
  </html>
);

export default layout;
```

```tsx
import type { Page } from "fadeno-framework-internal";
import { routeHref } from "fadeno:routes";
import { projectSummary } from "../resources/projects.ts";

const greetingHref = routeHref({ route: "/hello/[name]", parameters: { name: "Reader" } });

const page: Page = async ({ read }) => {
  const [first, equivalent] = await Promise.all([
    read(projectSummary, { projectId: 7, region: "north" }),
    read(projectSummary, { region: "north", projectId: 7 }),
  ]);
  if (first !== equivalent) throw new Error("equivalent resource reads did not share one result");

  return (
    <section aria-labelledby="welcome-heading">
      <h1 id="welcome-heading">First running Fadeno application</h1>
      <p>This document is routed, escaped, and streamed without client JavaScript.</p>
      <p>Project {first.projectId} is ready for {first.viewer}.</p>
      <p>Equivalent resource reads shared one request result.</p>
      <a href={greetingHref}>Open the parameterized greeting</a>
    </section>
  );
};

export default page;
```

## Check, develop, build, and start

Run `pnpm check:v1-analyzer-workflow` at the repository root to execute the
packed human `fadeno check` success, failure, explanation, and recovery paths.
Run `pnpm --dir examples/v1-app dev` for the demonstrated loopback development
workflow. Native mutation submission intentionally remains unavailable over
that HTTP listener because production actions require an exact HTTPS origin.

Run `pnpm check:v1-running-example` to fresh-pack the framework, create clean
consumers, produce two byte-identical builds, start the verified production
bootstrap, exercise routes/resources/actions, and prove rollback and stale
output removal. A manual production start additionally supplies `FADENO_PORT`,
an exact HTTPS `FADENO_ORIGIN`, and an active-first `FADENO_SESSION_KEYS`
keyring as described by the canonical application's README.
